trace_summary.task_objective: A fixed three-hop retrieval pipeline over Wikipedia abstracts. It performs exactly three retrievals and returns the concatenation of everything retrieved. The claim is: 'This athlete played for The New York Jets, two years after he was drafted. He was re-acquired in the 2015 New York Jets season.'
trace_summary.final_output_summary: 24 documents returned across three hops. Hop 1 retrieved 7 documents including Jason Wiltz, Justin Miller, Devin Smith, and Kris Jenkins. Hop 2 retrieved 7 documents including the '2015 New York Jets season' article mentioning Darrelle Revis and Antonio Cromartie were re-acquired. Hop 3 retrieved 10 documents. The pipeline completed all three hops as specified.
trace_summary.summary: The three-hop retrieval pipeline executed as specified, completing all three retrievals and returning 24 concatenated documents. Hop 1 used the claim verbatim and retrieved several Jets players. The summarizer correctly identified that none matched all criteria. The query generator for hop 2 produced a detailed query about 2015 Jets re-acquisitions, which successfully retrieved the '2015 New York Jets season' document mentioning Darrelle Revis and Antonio Cromartie. The summarizer noted these names but lacked their draft information. The query generator for hop 3 produced a more focused query. All four generated steps executed their structural obligations correctly. The pipeline's design does not include verification of claim truth or deduplication, so the presence of duplicate documents and the absence of a verdict are not failures. The system retrieved relevant documents including the key '2015 New York Jets season' article that names the re-acquired players.
